bio.en: A former actress who became Justinian's wife and co-ruler; during the Nika riots she persuaded him not to flee, saving his throne.
The most celebrated Sasanian ruler, who reformed taxes and the army, fought Byzantium and patronised learning.
Founder of Islam who united the Arabian tribes under a new faith; the revelations he received form the Quran.
Regent who promoted Buddhism and Chinese-style government in Japan and is credited with the Seventeen-Article Constitution.
Second Tang emperor, whose reign is seen as a golden age that made Tang China the greatest power in Asia.
Cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad and the fourth caliph; Shia Muslims revere him as the first Imam.
A monk who spent 17 years travelling through Central Asia and India, bringing hundreds of Buddhist texts back to China.
Ruled the Maya city of Palenque for 68 years; his tomb in the Temple of the Inscriptions is a landmark of Maya archaeology.
The only woman in Chinese history to rule as emperor in her own right, founding her own Zhou dynasty.
A princess from Dos Pilas who restored the power of Naranjo, ruling and waging war as a full sovereign.
Alongside Du Fu, China's greatest poet; his verses on wine, the moon and wandering are known to every Chinese schoolchild.

role.en: emperor who founded Heian-kyō, the future Kyoto

bio.en: Reigned 781–806. To escape the grip of Nara's Buddhist temples he moved the capital to Nagaoka (784) and then, in 794, to Heian-kyō, which stayed the capital for over a thousand years; he sent Sakanoue no Tamuramaro against the Emishi in the north.
United much of Western Europe and was crowned emperor in 800, sparking the Carolingian Renaissance.
Fifth Abbasid caliph under whom Baghdad became the richest city in the world; a hero of the Thousand and One Nights.

role.en: Charlemagne's son, under whom his empire began to break up

bio.en: Charlemagne's only surviving son and emperor from 814. His attempts to divide the realm among his sons provoked revolts and, after his death, the partition of the empire by the Treaty of Verdun in 843.
Scholar of Baghdad's House of Wisdom whose treatise gave algebra its name; the word 'algorithm' comes from his name.

Leading teacher of Advaita Vedanta: only Brahman is truly real and the self (atman) is identical with it; the world's multiplicity is illusion (maya). Tradition credits him with founding four monasteries across India.

Worked at Baghdad's House of Wisdom, where Greek authors were translated. The first Arab thinker to bring Aristotelian and Neoplatonic philosophy into dialogue with Islam; he also wrote on mathematics, music and ciphers.

role.en: first king of West Francia, the future France

bio.en: Under the Treaty of Verdun (843) he received the western part of Charlemagne's empire, from which France grew. He fought Viking raids throughout his reign and was crowned emperor in Rome in 875.

role.en: Varangian prince, founder of the Rurik dynasty

bio.en: A Varangian chieftain who, according to the Primary Chronicle, was invited to rule Novgorod in 862. All the princes of Rus and the Muscovite tsars until 1598 traced their descent from him.

role.en: prince who united Novgorod and Kiev and campaigned against Constantinople

bio.en: Around 882 he seized Kiev, killing Askold and Dir, and made it the capital of Rus. After a campaign against Constantinople in 907 he concluded an advantageous treaty with Byzantium in 911.

role.en: King of Wessex who held off the Vikings

bio.en: King of Wessex who defeated the Vikings at Edington in 878. He built a network of fortified burhs, created a fleet, issued a law code and promoted translations of books into Old English.
Joined the philosophy of Aristotle and Plato with Islamic thought; his Virtuous City describes an ideal state led by a philosopher-ruler. He was called the "Second Teacher", after Aristotle.
Originally a Mu'tazilite, around the age of forty he broke with them and began defending traditional Sunni doctrine with rational argument. His school of kalam became the dominant one in Sunni Islam.

role.en: Alfred's son who won back East Anglia and Mercia from the Danes

bio.en: Son of Alfred the Great. With his sister Æthelflæd he recovered East Anglia and the Midlands from the Danes and took over Mercia, paving the way for a united England.

role.en: prince of Kiev killed by the Drevlians over a second tribute

bio.en: Son of Rurik and husband of Princess Olga. He led campaigns against Byzantium in 941 and 944 and concluded a treaty with it; in 945 he was killed by the Drevlians while trying to collect tribute from them a second time.

role.en: first king of all England, victor at Brunanburh

bio.en: Grandson of Alfred the Great. He took York in 927, becoming the first ruler of all England, and in 937 crushed an alliance of Scots and Vikings at the Battle of Brunanburh.

role.en: founder of the Holy Roman Empire who crushed the Magyars at the Lech

bio.en: King of East Francia from 936, he routed the Magyars on the Lech in 955 and was crowned emperor in Rome by Pope John XII in 962 — the coronation usually taken as the birth of the Holy Roman Empire.
Ruled Rus' after her husband Igor's death, taking brutal revenge on the Drevlians; the first Rus' ruler to accept Christianity.
Author of the Shahnameh, the vast national epic of Iran that he spent some thirty years writing.
Duke of the Franks, elected king in 987 after the death of the last Carolingian, Louis V. His male-line descendants ruled France until 1848.
Warrior prince who destroyed the Khazar Khaganate and fought Byzantium on the Danube.

role.en: king of a peaceful united England and patron of monastic reform

bio.en: His reign passed without major wars. He backed the Benedictine reform of the monasteries, and his coronation at Bath in 973 became the model for all later English coronations.

role.en: emperor wed to the Byzantine Theophanu, defeated by the Arabs in Calabria

bio.en: Son of Otto I, married to the Byzantine princess Theophanu. In 982 he was badly defeated by the Sicilian Arabs at Cape Colonna and died in Rome a year later — the only emperor buried in St Peter's.

role.en: prince of Kiev who fell in a civil war with his brother Vladimir

bio.en: Eldest son of Sviatoslav. He began the first civil war in Rus, in which his brother Oleg died; he was then defeated by his brother Vladimir and killed on his orders.
In 988 he made Rus' Christian, adopting the faith from Byzantium; remembered in epic songs as 'Vladimir the Fair Sun'.
Lady-in-waiting to the empress and author of The Pillow Book, a masterpiece of Heian Japanese prose.

role.en: king who paid off the Vikings with Danegeld

bio.en: He tried to buy off Viking raids with huge payments of Danegeld and in 1002 ordered the massacre of Danes in England. In 1013 he fled from Sweyn Forkbeard to Normandy but later regained the throne.
Icelandic Norseman who reached North America around 1000 AD, nearly five centuries before Columbus.

role.en: pious king excommunicated for marrying a kinswoman

bio.en: Son of Hugh Capet, crowned co-king as early as 987. His marriage to his cousin Bertha of Burgundy brought excommunication; after a long war he brought Burgundy under the crown.
Khwarazmian polymath who measured the Earth's radius and wrote a monumental study of India.

role.en: novelist, author of The Tale of Genji

bio.en: A court lady who wrote The Tale of Genji, often called the world's first novel.

role.en: last Ottonian emperor, founder of the see of Bamberg, canonised as a saint

bio.en: The last emperor of the Ottonian dynasty. He founded the bishopric of Bamberg in 1007 and fought long wars with Bolesław the Brave of Poland; in 1146 he was canonised — the only German king to be made a saint, as was his wife Cunigunde.
Under him Kievan Rus' flourished: he issued the Russkaya Pravda law code and built St Sophia's Cathedral.
Physician and philosopher whose Canon of Medicine was the standard medical textbook in the East and Europe for centuries.

role.en: boy emperor who dreamed of reviving the Roman Empire with its seat in Rome

bio.en: King at three and emperor in 996, he proclaimed a "renewal of the Roman Empire", settled in Rome, visited Gniezno in 1000 and opened Charlemagne's tomb in Aachen; he died aged 21.

role.en: prince of Kiev blamed by the chronicles for murdering Boris and Gleb

bio.en: He seized Kiev after Vladimir's death in 1015; the chronicle blames him for murdering his brothers Boris and Gleb, who became the first Russian saints. Defeated by Yaroslav on the Alta in 1019, he fled.

role.en: first Salian emperor, who added the Kingdom of Burgundy to the empire

bio.en: Founder of the Salian dynasty. In 1033 he joined the Kingdom of Burgundy to the empire, began Speyer Cathedral as the Salian burial church, and in 1037 issued an edict making the fiefs of lesser vassals hereditary.

role.en: Danish king who ruled a North Sea empire

bio.en: Danish prince who conquered England in 1016. He united England, Denmark and Norway under his rule, governing firmly but peacefully with the support of the English nobility and church.
